## P3801 — A plaintext default ADMIN password is published in a migration and its account exists in production (suspended) - rotate it, do NOT edit the migration (Prisma checksums applied migrations)

**EXPOSURE, VERIFIED MYSELF in production and in the repo, 2026-10-14.** `backend/prisma/migrations/20251104_seed_admin_user/migration.sql` (in `C:\Users\ezabz\Code\phone-and-tech-full`, the LIVE clone) **states a plaintext default admin password in a comment**, with the matching bcrypt hash in the INSERT below it. The account it creates, **`admin@test.com` (`users.id` 1, role ADMIN), EXISTS in production** - `SUSPENDED`, and that suspension is the only thing preventing use of a credential that is published in the repository. `manager@test.com` (`users.id` 2, role MANAGER) is in the same state. Measured: `admin@test.com` SUSPENDED, `manager@test.com` SUSPENDED, `ai-admin@lakewoodphoneandtech.com` (id 168, ADMIN) ACTIVE, `agent-verification@lakewoodphoneandtech.com` (id 300, MANAGER) ACTIVE.

**The naive fix is WRONG and would have broken the deploy pipeline.** The reconnaissance recommended "deleting the credential from the migration". That migration is **already applied**, and Prisma stores a **checksum** per applied migration in `_prisma_migrations` - editing the file changes the checksum and can make `migrate deploy` refuse with a drift error. **Do not edit an applied migration to remove a secret; rotate the secret.**

**OWNER DECISION 2026-10-14: rotate both accounts, and let `lpt-web` be the thing that does it** - asked as a direct question with the recommendation to rotate immediately in the admin UI, and he chose to wait for the tool. So the rotation is now a **hard acceptance requirement of the `lpt-web` build** and its **first applied production action**, and the manager (not the builder) runs it once the tool is verified.

**Why this matters beyond the two accounts:** a credential published in a repository is not protected by anything except a status flag in a table, and status flags get flipped - by a reconciliation, an admin, or a script. And the deeper pattern: **test/seed accounts must not exist in production at all.** `admin@test.com` and `manager@test.com` are seed fixtures from a migration that was written for CI and initial setup and then run against the live database. Two accounts in a production user table are named after a test domain, and the only reason this is not an incident is that somebody suspended them.

**Where it is tracked:** the `lpt-web` build (mesh child, design `_scratch/web-parity/DESIGN.md`, recon `_scratch/web-parity/A-RECON.md`) carries it as a definition-of-done item; the amendment telling the builder not to apply it themselves and to report the role gate is in that child's thread. **This entry exists so the rotation cannot be lost if that session dies** - if you are reading this and the rotation has not happened, do it, and say so.
